//: Turbo façade for geoai-core. This file exists so turbo can reach the package; every command it runs is a Python tool from the pixi environment, and the commands themselves belong in the package's pyproject.toml and pixi.toml. Two rules make it work. (1) Always `cd` to the repository root first: ruff's `src` and pytest's `testpaths` in pyproject.toml are absolute-from-root, so a command run from inside python/geoai-core resolves neither. (2) Never invoke a tool through node_modules/.bin — those entries carry a `node` shebang, and no environment in this repository provides node; bun is the only JavaScript runtime, and the tools below are conda dependencies resolved from pixi.lock. Keys prefixed `//` are the convention for commenting in package.json: bun parses it as strict JSON, so a raw `#` comment is a syntax error.
name: @geoaiworkbench/core

scripts.lint: cd ../.. && ruff check python/geoai-core && ruff format --check python/geoai-core
scripts.fmt: cd ../.. && ruff check --fix python/geoai-core && ruff format python/geoai-core

//cov: COVERAGE_FILE is not optional. turbo runs all three cov tasks concurrently in the same working directory, and coverage's default data file is the single path ./.coverage — so the three runs interleave writes to one SQLite file and each report ends up containing every package's numbers (observed: geoai-core's report listing all three packages, geoai-mcp's listing two). The numbers stay plausible, which is the dangerous part: nothing looks wrong, the merged total is just wrong. One data file per package is the fix; a per-package data_file in pyproject.toml would work too but is invisible at the point where the collision happens.
